<a name="ObjectCache"></a>
## type [ObjectCache](<https://github.com/blanketops/environments/blob/main/cache/objectcache.go#L35-L39>)

ObjectCache provides namespace\-aware, generation\-scoped field caching for a single CR kind. Domain caches embed this and add typed helpers.

Keys: \<kind\>:\<namespace\>/\<name\>:gen\<generation\>:\<field\> Generation scoping means a spec change naturally orphans stale entries \(they expire via TTL\) — no invalidation hook required, and it works identically on backends without key enumeration \(Memcached\).

```go
type ObjectCache struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

```go
func NewObjectCache(c *corecache.Cache, kind string, ttl time.Duration) *ObjectCache
```

NewObjectCache constructs an ObjectCache scoped to the given CR kind, with fields expiring after ttl \(0 disables expiry\).

<a name="ObjectCache.Invalidate"></a>
### func \(\*ObjectCache\) [Invalidate](<https://github.com/blanketops/environments/blob/main/cache/objectcache.go#L73>)

```go
func (o *ObjectCache) Invalidate(ctx context.Context, nn types.NamespacedName) error
```

Invalidate drops all cached fields for an object \(all generations\). Call on delete events. Backends without enumeration no\-op; generation scoping already protects correctness there.
